title: Some things I think I think, Preseason Game 3 edition. 1) Athan Kaliakmanis got a lot of national attention for his play in Detroit. I think he impressed with how he slung the ball. I'd imagine he will start tonight in Baltimore. If he plays well, does the WSH staff feel like they need to keep him on the 53 man roster to protect him? 2) Who is squarely on the bubble right now? It feels like the DT spot is competitive from a last-man-in standpoint. Cowart 55, Barber 50, Hurst 77 are all players to watch. They've all had really good preseasons. 3) Is Luke McCaffrey definitively on this team? I don't think McLaurin, Diggs, Williams or even Lane need to play tonight. Does Luke get treated like those guys or is he going to be running around with the "something to prove" group. 4) What's the deal at LB. Can you keep all of your athletic, fast off-ball backers? Luvu, Styles and Chenal are locks. I think Magee, Kaho and Medrano are all potential special teams weapons who can move well enough to help on defense. Who's in and who's out tonight. 5) I think they are keeping 4 TEs. If that's true, and they end up keeping 3 QB's, what position group pays the price? You can't be heavy everywhere. If you're keeping 10 DL and 6 LB's then you have to be stingy in the secondary. Could they keep an OL fewer than people think?
summary:
Some things I think I think, Preseason Game 3 edition. 

1) Athan Kaliakmanis got a lot of national attention for his play in Detroit. I think he impressed with how he slung the ball. I'd imagine he will start tonight in Baltimore. If he plays well, does the WSH staff feel like they need to keep him on the 53 man roster to protect him? 

2) Who is squarely on the bubble right now? It feels like the DT spot is competitive from a last-man-in standpoint. Cowart 55, Barber 50, Hurst 77 are all players to watch. They've all had really good preseasons. 

3) Is Luke McCaffrey definitively on this team? I don't think McLaurin, Diggs, Williams or even Lane need to play tonight. Does Luke get treated like those guys or is he going to be running around with the "something to prove" group. 

4) What's the deal at LB. Can you keep all of your athletic, fast off-ball backers? Luvu, Styles and Chenal are locks. I think Magee, Kaho and Medrano are all potential special teams weapons who can move well enough to help on defense. Who's in and who's out tonight. 

5) I think they are keeping 4 TEs. If that's true, and they end up keeping 3 QB's, what position group pays the price? You can't be heavy everywhere. If you're keeping 10 DL and 6 LB's then you have to be stingy in the secondary. Could they keep an OL fewer than people think?

1) Athan Kaliakmanis got a lot of national attention for his play in Detroit. I think he impressed with how he slung the ball. I'd imagine he will start tonight in Baltimore. If he plays well, does the WSH staff feel like they need to keep him on the 53 man roster to protect him? 

2) Who is squarely on the bubble right now? It feels like the DT spot is competitive from a last-man-in standpoint. Cowart 55, Barber 50, Hurst 77 are all players to watch. They've all had really good preseasons. 

3) Is Luke McCaffrey definitively on this team? I don't think McLaurin, Diggs, Williams or even Lane need to play tonight. Does Luke get treated like those guys or is he going to be running around with the "something to prove" group. 

4) What's the deal at LB. Can you keep all of your athletic, fast off-ball backers? Luvu, Styles and Chenal are locks. I think Magee, Kaho and Medrano are all potential special teams weapons who can move well enough to help on defense. Who's in and who's out tonight. 

5) I think they are keeping 4 TEs. If that's true, and they end up keeping 3 QB's, what position group pays the price? You can't be heavy everywhere. If you're keeping 10 DL and 6 LB's then you have to be stingy in the secondary. Could they keep an OL fewer than people think?

title: Ravens wrap up preseason tonight vs. Commanders with 6PM kickoff at M&T Bank Stadium. Biggest storyline for the Ravens’ preseason finale … Center position battle Jovaughn Gwyn has been working with the starters since Danny Pinter suffered a season-ending knee injury. But Gwyn hasn’t started an NFL game in his three-year career and has played a total of 11 offensive snaps. Ethan Pocic, the most experienced center on the roster, was expected to get some reps with the first team this week but that hasn’t materialized. Pocic has to prove he’s fully recovered from a torn Achilles that he suffered in December. It will be interesting to see who starts and how much playing time each gets tonight. Ravens OC Declan Doyle said earlier this week: "I feel like we have two really good options there. Obviously, [I] was really excited about Danny [Pinter] and the direction that he was kind of pushing. But we will continue to evaluate that spot, and we will make a decision here as we go.”

title: Pet peeve with 53-man roster projections: Putting TBD (or player not on roster) in the roster count. That’s not how initial 53s work unless you think they’ll cut to 52 (that happens like maybe once a year). More than a 96% chance the team will cut down to 53 and not leave a spot open. I get why the TBD is there but if you’re doing an initial 53 that feels unlikely. (Genuinely not subtweeting anyone, just a Kaye’s Take)

Whichever quarterback they seem to be trying to protect more could be the answer as to who has won the backup spot ** The Tight Ends: I have started to talk myself into Stone Smartt making the roster. If he has a big game tonight I might have to put him on my final 53-man roster prediction. The Eagles really need one of their backup tight ends to step up with Eli Stowers hurt. ** Where is Mannion?: Mannion will be calling the game from either the booth or the field tonight. Whichever one he picks is likely where he will be in Week 1.

title: Sorry to get a little bit gushy on this app, but it's Olivia's 9th birthday! I think about that dumb line from The Office, "I wish there was a way to know you're in the good old days before you've actually left them” a lot while raising Olivia. Because I am acutely aware that I am in the good old days with Olivia. And I keep expecting those good old days to fade as Olivia gets older, but they haven’t, and I feel extremely grateful about that. Olivia is an absolutely incredible kid, and I truly cherish — nearly — every moment I get to spend with her, because let’s be honest, being a parent isn’t without its occasional challenges. But I feel so lucky to have a kid like Olivia who I truly, genuinely love being around. I want to bring her everywhere. I wish she didn’t have to go to school, so we could just hang out all day. She’s funny, she’s silly, she’s thoughtful, she’s kind, she’s smart, she’s brave, she’s well-mannered, she speaks her mind, and she’s really cute! She doesn’t care about most of my interests. She doesn’t know the rules of baseball or football. She has no interest in the Beach Boys, punk or hardcore or late-60s, early-70s country rock, and she thought Dumb & Dumber was a terrible movie. But I can spend all day talking to her, we make each other laugh every single night when we play with her stuffed animals at bedtime, and we love talking about Hallie. And we do both enjoy a Disney park and arcade. I wish Olivia could be a little kid forever, but I love watching her grow and learn and improve. Love you, Olivia! You’re the GOAT. This is where Olivia usually says, “You’re an even bigger one!” But she’s wrong. She’s the biggest GOAT.

title: Some #49ers roster thoughts/questions now that preseason is (basically) over: - Can they live with Carver Willis growing pains early? It sure seems like he's got the inside track on the LG job. There's potential there but there will be bumps along the way. If Robert Jones is back soon, still wonder if he begins the year as starter with Willis waiting in the wings. - Who starts at DT next to Osa Odighizuwa? It's been an uninspiring camp/preseason for Collins and West. There are injury related reasons for both but still fair to wonder what they have there. There will be plenty of options for third down (White/Williams can kick inside) but early downs, they need someone to hold up against the run. West showed some of that late last year and they want Collins to take a step. Haven't seen it yet. James Thompson Jr. and Gracen Halton have some juice but obviously green. - The LB pecking order is tough to decipher. Warner, Greenlaw are obvious. Dugger, too. It seems Wallow has carved out a role and Bethune is still in the mix but there's a lot to figure out given injuries to Nick Martin and Luke Gifford. - Posed the question the other day but is Drake Nugent the backup C? Brett Toth still not back from concussion, Nugent has had a solid camp. Have to have someone who can handle the job. - Is there enough at safety? Still a lot of questions there and though Malik Mustapha has been doing a lot of running on the side (and was getting his GPS checked as recently as Tuesday), that competition never really formed. An improved pass rush would help them but this spot, DT and LG are still biggest questions on the roster when it comes to starters, IMO.

- Who starts at DT next to Osa Odighizuwa? It's been an uninspiring camp/preseason for Collins and West. There are injury related reasons for both but still fair to wonder what they have there. There will be plenty of options for third down (White/Williams can kick inside) but early downs, they need someone to hold up against the run. West showed some of that late last year and they want Collins to take a step. Haven't seen it yet. James Thompson Jr. and Gracen Halton have some juice but obviously green. 

- The LB pecking order is tough to decipher. Warner, Greenlaw are obvious. Dugger, too. It seems Wallow has carved out a role and Bethune is still in the mix but there's a lot to figure out given injuries to Nick Martin and Luke Gifford. 

- Posed the question the other day but is Drake Nugent the backup C? Brett Toth still not back from concussion, Nugent has had a solid camp. Have to have someone who can handle the job. 

- Is there enough at safety? Still a lot of questions there and though Malik Mustapha has been doing a lot of running on the side (and was getting his GPS checked as recently as Tuesday), that competition never really formed. An improved pass rush would help them but this spot, DT and LG are still biggest questions on the roster when it comes to starters, IMO.

- Can they live with Carver Willis growing pains early? It sure seems like he's got the inside track on the LG job. There's potential there but there will be bumps along the way. If Robert Jones is back soon, still wonder if he begins the year as starter with Willis waiting in the wings. 

- Who starts at DT next to Osa Odighizuwa? It's been an uninspiring camp/preseason for Collins and West. There are injury related reasons for both but still fair to wonder what they have there. There will be plenty of options for third down (White/Williams can kick inside) but early downs, they need someone to hold up against the run. West showed some of that late last year and they want Collins to take a step. Haven't seen it yet. James Thompson Jr. and Gracen Halton have some juice but obviously green. 

- The LB pecking order is tough to decipher. Warner, Greenlaw are obvious. Dugger, too. It seems Wallow has carved out a role and Bethune is still in the mix but there's a lot to figure out given injuries to Nick Martin and Luke Gifford. 

- Posed the question the other day but is Drake Nugent the backup C? Brett Toth still not back from concussion, Nugent has had a solid camp. Have to have someone who can handle the job. 

- Is there enough at safety? Still a lot of questions there and though Malik Mustapha has been doing a lot of running on the side (and was getting his GPS checked as recently as Tuesday), that competition never really formed.
